title: FDA-Approved Drug Repurposing as p53 Mutants Rescue Candidates Using Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Molecular Simulations.
one_liner_zh: 该文用结构虚拟筛选和分子动力学模拟筛选FDA药物稳定突变p53，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作背景但核心是蛋白-配体结合，非TF-DNA互作建模，方法可迁移但对象偏离。
abstract: The restoration of mutant p53 stability is a highly sought-after strategy in targeted cancer therapy. This study presents a structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics approach to nominate FDA-approved drugs as candidate stabilizers of mutant p53 for downstream experimental validation. A virtual screening library of FDA-approved compounds was docked against three representative p53 mutants (7DHY, 7DHZ, and 7V97) to evaluate their binding potential. The prioritized candidates demonstrated consistent, multi-conformer binding affinities. Protein-ligand interaction profiling revealed that the candidate DB09280 possesses a highly dense interaction network, particularly against the V272M and R249S variants. Residue-level analysis of the G245S structural mutant showed that DB09280 uniquely engages His19, a crucial residue for zinc coordination, and forms stabilizing contacts with adjacent flexible loop residues, including ASN35 and PRO32. Subsequent 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations were consistent with DB09280 acting as a putative conformational clamp on the timescale sampled. The ligand-bound (holo) system exhibited substantially reduced global structural drift (RMSD) and attenuated local residue fluctuation (RMSF) within the core domain compared to the highly unstable apo state. Principal component analysis further indicated that DB09280 restricts the broad conformational sampling of the mutant into a stable, dominant basin within the sampled trajectory. Together, these computational findings nominate DB09280 as a promising candidate structural stabilizer of mutant p53 worthy of experimental follow-up. We emphasize that the in silico stabilization observed here is not equivalent to functional rescue of p53 transcriptional activity; biochemical, biophysical, and cell-based assays will be required to establish whether DB09280 restores wild-type-like DNA binding or tumor-suppressor function in mutant p53 contexts.
abstract_zh: 恢复突变型p53的稳定性是靶向癌症治疗中备受追求的策略。本研究采用基于结构的虚拟筛选和分子动力学方法，提名FDA批准的药物作为突变型p53的候选稳定剂，以供下游实验验证。将FDA批准化合物的虚拟筛选库对接至三种代表性p53突变体（7DHY、7DHZ和7V97），以评估其结合潜力。优先候选物表现出一致的多构象结合亲和力。蛋白质-配体相互作用分析显示，候选物DB09280具有高度密集的相互作用网络，尤其针对V272M和R249S变体。对G245S结构突变体的残基水平分析表明，DB09280独特地结合His19（锌配位的关键残基），并与相邻柔性环残基（包括ASN35和PRO32）形成稳定接触。随后的500 ns分子动力学模拟与DB09280在采样时间尺度上作为推定构象钳的作用一致。与高度不稳定的无配体（apo）状态相比，配体结合（holo）系统在核心结构域内表现出显著降低的整体结构漂移（RMSD）和减弱的局部残基波动（RMSF）。主成分分析进一步表明，DB09280将突变体的广泛构象采样限制在采样轨迹内的稳定主导盆地中。综合这些计算发现，DB09280被提名为突变型p53的有前景候选结构稳定剂，值得实验跟进。我们强调，此处观察到的计算机模拟稳定化并不等同于p53转录活性的功能恢复；需要生化、生物物理和基于细胞的检测来确定DB09280是否在突变型p53背景下恢复野生型样DNA结合或肿瘤抑制功能。
